detail.longDescription: Most of my homelab runs in Docker — easy to rebuild, easy to move between hosts. Home Assistant is the one exception: it stays bare-metal on its own box, no container layer between it and the Zigbee/USB hardware it talks to. That isolation means a container restart elsewhere never risks dropping a light automation mid-flight, at the cost of one more OS to patch by hand. Some services are worth keeping outside the blast radius of everything else. # HomeAssistant # Docker # homelab # selfhosted
